text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Serious divisions have emerged among senior government officials on whether or not to invite international tenders for the implementation of multi-million-dollar plans to develop domestic airports, sources told the Financial Gazette this week.

- Zimbabwe's office of the comptroller and auditor-general has questioned the circumstances under which a former War Victims Compensation Fund commissioner, who was dismissed by the government in May, was paid over Z$100,000 from the fund.

- A group of black Zimbabwean pilots have locked horns with the transport and energy ministry over their plans to start an aviation school for blacks, to reverse the current white domination of the industry.

- Zimbabwe's black economic empowerment pressure group, the Affirmative Action Group, has called for meaningful black empowerment in the operations of companies like Coca Cola, Bata Shoe Company, Rothmans and BP Shell.

- IBM Zimbabwe, which was under pressure from the government to localise 30 percent of its equity or risk having its licence to operate in the country revoked, has opted to establish an Employee Trust to take up the 30 percent, rather than sell the shares to local black businesses.
- British investors could pour over Z$8 billion worth of fresh investments over the next five years into Zimbabwe, creating thousands of new jobs in various sectors of industry and commerce.

- The World Bank on Thursday said it had formally advised the Zimbabwean government of an approval to release Z$720 million in balance of payment support for the southern African country's economic reform programme.
